walkthroughs.body_html:
World Focus Music Study — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World Focus Music Study brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World Focus Music Study.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Reusing audio in a new track is called?
options: Mixing
Sampling
Mastering
Tracking

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: It is the same as the chorus.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.
It is the very first section.

mcqs.q: What three notes form a major triad in root position?
options: It is the very first section.
Root, major third, perfect fifth.
Three consecutive scale notes.
Any three notes played together.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets are in a semibreve?
options: It is the very first section.

Digital Audio Workstation (e.g., Logic, Ableton) used for recording and producing music.
Chord progression I-IV-V over 12 bars; underpins blues, rock and roll.
Common pop structure alternating verses and a memorable repeated chorus.
